Commentary.Commentary: Right then! A number 1 T20I team taking on a young and inexperienced Protean side with key players rested. You would have expected Pakistan to be 2-0 up. But South Africa have turned the tables with a role reversal and however one might say Pakistan choked, the Protea bowlers deserve no less credit for their efforts. Can they now produce a dream result of whitewashing the number 1 side? Or will Pakistan leave the African shores with something to smile about? Join us on Wednesday, February 6, 2019 at 6 pm local (1600 GMT) for all the action from the third and final T20I in Centurion. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

VICTORIOUS SOUTH AFRICAN SKIPPER DAVID MILLER HAS BEEN NAMED THE MAN OF THE MATCH FOR HIS 65 (29). Is all smiles about the result and praises his bowlers for doing incredibly well. On his own batting in the final over, Miller says that it was very enjoyable. Since it was the last over, he says that he just tried swinging. After connecting the first 2 balls, he felt that he could get a few more. Admits that South Africa did not start too well with the ball but then came back superbly at the back end. Praises Sipamla for doing really well on debut. On his thought process with Pakistan's score reading 63/1 after 5 overs, David says that he felt he was the worst captain in history but then smiles and says that he just asked the bowlers to keep working on the cutters and try and execute them.

Pakistan captain, Shoaib Malik says that it was an exceptional game but is disappointed that Pakistan could not win in spite of having it on a platter. On Babar Azam, he says that Babar is a class player, playing proper cricketing shots. Praises Hussain Talat as well and again laments that despite their heroic efforts, the rest of the team could not finish it off. But also criticizes them a bit saying that one of the two should have finished the game off because it becomes difficult for a new batsman to face the old ball. However, he understands that T20 is a game of risks and adds that the team needs to sit in the dressing room and analyze how to finish off matches. Praises Imad Wasim and Shaheen Afridi for bowling superbly in the Powerplay but laments again that the death overs cost them. Admits that he was wary that a big David Miller knock was always around the corner and they had different backup plans for his attack but they could not materialize. Overall, he says that Pakistan need to plan better for the last few overs. On the third match, Malik says that every game presents itself with a new opportunity. What is gone is gone and Pakistan just need to focus on trying to win the third and final T20I, learning from what has happened in the first 2 games.

This match could have been won by anyone. But in such games, the team which holds its nerves comes out trumps. Pakistan should have not have been chasing more than 170 with South Africa 126/3 after 16.1 overs. The tourists should have won with 42 needed from 24 balls. But there lies the main difference - South Africa finished the innings nicely with the bat and finished the game exceedingly well with the ball. Majority of the bowlers got hammered but a word for the debutant Lutho Sipamla - his 4-0-23-0 along with Shamsi's 4-0-31-0 kept Pakistan quiet for a while in the middle overs and in T20 cricket, many times, even 2-3 good overs can put some pressure. Please stay tuned for the presentation...

When Azam got out, Pakistan needed 42 from 23 balls. 8 wickets were left in the tank. Add to it, South Africa were not bowling well at all. But then, things started to happen. Pakistan kept losing wicket after wicket, inspite of getting a reprieve - Asif Ali being caught at 3 but the delivery being deemed a no ball. Yet, the best of spells came towards the end from the Proteas - Chris Morris bowled a stunning 19th over, where he picked up 2 wickets while Andile Phehlukwayo sealed the deal in the final over with the wicket of Shoaib Malik.

A 45-run stand between Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam in 24 balls set the platform for the win and then a 102-run partnership between Babar and Hussain Talat just nearly sealed the deal. NEARLY. How important is that adverb. The game is not over till it is over and today was another example of that.

A good start is always essential for a good result but you need a clinical finish to achieve that good result. Pakistan started well with the ball, but Miller's assault at the death literally killed them. And then, if we say the visitors exploded with the bat in the Powerplay, they imploded towards the end, committing suicide at the death.

A fantastic match. South Africa will say they bowled well to change the game from a losing position while Pakistan will opine that they let the opportunity slip by. Their string of 11 successive T20I series wins is broken. And how? First, a loss by 6 runs. Here, a loss by 7 runs. Nothing much to choose from.

South Africa. Choking. Go hand in hand, don't they? This time though, they have choked the opposition. Pakistan, being Pakistan, have played like Pakistan and lost like how, usually South Africa do, but then Pakistan can do anything because they are Pakistan. Mickey Arthur is stunned. Imagine you are about to take a bite of your favourite pizza and the whole box itself disappears.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single. SOUTH AFRICA WIN BY 7 RUNS AND TAKE AN UNASSAILABLE 2-0 SERIES LEAD!
Mohammad Rizwan eventually walks out now, with the game literally over.

OUT! BOWLED! That is the end of the game, theoretically. Phehlukwayo started this over badly but is taking full control of the same. Keeps it full and straight, expecting Hasan Ali to slog and that is exactly what Hasan does. He misses, Phehlukwayo hits. Bang. At the base of leg stump. What a choke from Pakistan - 6/33 in 23 balls!
Shadab Khan comes in now, at number 8, replacing his captain.

OUT! Is that the game for South Africa? Malik is gone now and with that, the chances of Pakistan winning as well. A length ball, around off, Shoaib gives this the kitchen sink, heaving with all his might. Gets it high in the air but not quite the distance. Rassie van der Dussen waits for the ball to complete the parabolic trajectory at deep mid-wicket and takes it comfortably. Then exults! 9 needed from 2...
Very full outside off, squeezed out to cover for a run. 9 from 3...
Misses out. Short and outside off, cut straight to point for just a single. 10 from 4 then.
FOUR! Well, Malik might finish things off! Full and straight, Malik gives himself room to the leg side and hammers it down the ground. Long on cannot get across in time! 11 needed from 5...
Hasan Ali comes in at number 7, replacing Imad. Interesting. No Rizwan. Andile Phehlukwayo has the responsibility of finishing things off.

OUT! The stumps are out of the ground! Second wicket in the over and both in the form of bowled. A length ball, outside off, coming in with the angle, Wasim has an almighty heave. But connects with thin air. The ball demolishes the stumps! Super over from Morris - 12 runs and 2 wickets. 3-0-36-2 for him.
FOUR! Up and over! Full and outside off, Imad backs away and lofts it cleanly over mid off!
Full on middle, driven down the ground. David Miller races to his right from long on, slides and returns the ball. Two runs taken.
Imad Wasim comes in at number 6, replacing Talat.

OUT! DRAGS IT ON! The game and series are slipping away from Pakistan. Full and around off, coming in, Talat swings wildly but a touch too early. He only manages a thin contact on the ball and unfortunately for him, it is an inside edge. The ball deflects and crashes into the stumps. Talat departs for 55. Big wicket. 21 needed from 9...
Outside off, Hussain swings hard but the ball goes off the inner half towards long on. That helps him as he races back for the second.
FOUR! Full toss outside off, Talat backs away and smashes it wide of mid off for a boundary! 23 more needed from 11 balls now!
Chris Morris is back on. 2-0-24-0 so far.
Outside off, pushed through point for one. Excellent over from Andile.
Full and outside off, lofted over cover for a run.
Length ball, slapped to deep cover for a single. Equation - 29 from 14.
WIDE! A full ball wide outside off, left alone.
Captain Shoaib Malik arrives at number 5, replacing Asif.

OUT! Asif holes out! A short ball, there to be hit, Ali pulls it with all his might but finds Reeza Hendricks to perfection at the mid-wicket fence! Are Pakistan actually choking here? 31 more needed and they are running out of time...
Pushes this through mid on for a single.
FOUR! That will help Pakistan a bit! A length ball outside off, Talat throws his bat at it and gets a thick outside edge which flies through the vacant slip cordon to the third man fence!
Andile Phehlukwayo returns.

Huge shout for LBW, turned down. Probably height was the factor. A length ball outside off, coming in, Talat misses his swing and is hit on the pads. The ball deflects towards point and a leg bye is taken. Hawk Eye confirms that the ball was going over. No signal from the umpire, so must have been an inside edge as well.
Another play and a miss to a length ball outside off.
Superb ball. Sees Talat shuffling across and bowls a full ball, just around leg stump. Hussain looks to paddle but misses.
FREE HIT. Will this be costly for South Africa?

NO BALL! Asif Ali gets a reprieve! First of all, brilliant game awareness from him. When you play the game, you should abide by the rules. But to do so, you must KNOW the rules. It was a short ball outside off and Asif instinctively went for the pull. Got a top edge due to the extra bounce which went straight up in the air. Tabraiz Shamsi kept his eyes on it and took a fantastic catch. But Ali is not going anywhere. He reckons this should be a no ball for bouncing above the shoulder. Now, the umpires get together for a chat and then refer it upstairs. The first look in the replays tells us that it is above the shoulder. This could be another turning point...
Asif Ali has been caught! But is it a no ball for height? Referred upstairs...
Full and wide outside off, squeezed behind point for a couple. 150 COMES UP FOR PAKISTAN. 38 more needed from 21 balls.
A short ball, around middle, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a run.
WIDE. Sees Talat getting across his stumps and fires it down the leg side. Fires it too far down. Hussain misses his flick.
Asif Ali comes in at number 4, replacing Babar.

OUT! Caught! No century for Babar Azam! Is there gonna be a twist in the tale? A short ball, around off, Azam looks for the pull but gets too much height on the ball. The pace taken off does not aid his cause either. The ball hits the top half of the bat and goes high in the air, but does not have enough on it to clear the fence. Simple catch for Junior Dala at wide long on. Fantastic 90 by Babar. But will it prove to be enough? 42 more needed from 23 balls...
Beuran Hendricks is back on. 2-0-24-1 so far.
SIX! MURDERED! This time Talat connects. A short ball, another slower one, this time Hussain picks the change in pace, waits for it to come and pulls it over mid-wicket! 100-RUN STAND COMES UP!
Another dot! The off cutter outside off, on a length, HT swings this a million miles into the stratosphere but makes no contact.
Superb yorker, right on the line of off stump, dug out towards short third man. Just a run.
Full on middle, pushed down to long on for a single. 49 needed from 27 now. All of a sudden, pressure is building.
Lovely slower ball, outside off, Hussain swings but misses.

Flirting with the wide lines. Bowls an off cutter, does Morris, landing it around off, Talat lets it go, expecting it to cross the line from the over-the-wicket angle, but the ball just grazes that line. No wide given.
Chris Morris returns. 1-0-16-0 so far.
On middle and leg, heaved through mid-wicket for one more. 4-0-23-0 for Lutho Sipamla on debut. Sadly, it might not be enough for his side.

Well done, Reeza Hendricks. Sipamla appreciates that effort. On a length outside off, BA guides it between short third man and backward point. Hendricks from the latter position dives to his left and makes a stunning stop. Just a run.
WIDE. Sees Babar shuffle a bit and bowls it wide outside off. Azam smartly gets back to his original position after the ball is delivered and lets it go.
A short ball, neatly pulled through mid-wicket for one.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a run.
On middle, Babar swings hard but gets a thick inside edge behind to the keeper. The batsmen go through for the single and Klaasen fires a throw at the bowler's end but misses. Babar was a goner.
Lutho Sipamla is back on. 3-0-16-0 so far. Can he strike?
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Outside off, punched wide of mid off for a quick run.
Landed outside off, Hussain slashes but misses.
Outside off, a slash and a miss. Hussain admonishes himself.
FOUR! Cheeky. A length ball, around middle, Talat gets across and scoops it over short fine leg for a boundary! 59 more needed now, from 40 balls.
Full on middle, Azam chips it over the bowler for a single.
Junior Dala returns. 1-0-18-0 so far.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Around middle, helped through square leg for one.
FOUR! A lovely shot. A length ball outside off, Babar comes down the track and lofts it with finesse over cover for a boundary!
A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Short and around middle, worked through mid-wicket for a couple.
Andile Phehlukwayo is back on. 1-0-11-0 so far.
Full and on middle, swept straight to short fine leg.
That turns away a long way. Landed outside off, HT looks to push but the ball spins past the outside edge.
A long hop, pulled through mid-wicket for one.
Short and outside off, Hussain looks to cut but gets a thick outside edge which lands just short of point. A run taken.
FOUR! Fine shot. Full and around middle, Talat unfurls the reverse sweep and gets it over backward point for a boundary!
Full and around middle, worked through the leg side for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A short ball, pulled through mid-wicket for another single.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for one.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a run.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! MAGNIFICENT! Full and outside off, Talat drives this wide of cover for a boundary!
Lutho Sipamla is back on. 2-0-8-0 so far.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single. 14 from the over, 25 off the last 2! The run rate picks up again.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.

FOUR! Superbly done! Landed around off, spinning in, Babar goes back and cheekily dabs it, almost out of Klaasen's gloves, to the third man fence! FOURTH TIME IN THE GAME - Babar has scored a hat-trick of boundaries. First against Beuran Hendricks. Then against Chris Morris. Then Junior Dala. Now, Tabraiz Shamsi.
FOUR! Lovely shot. Full and around off, Azam comes down the track and lofts it over cover! 50-RUN STAND IS UP AS WELL!
FOUR! Nicely done. Full and around middle, Azam gets down and sweeps it fine, past short fine leg!
Full and around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
A length ball outside off, Babar slashes hard and gets a thick outside edge through the vacant slip region to the third man region. A run taken. 11 from the over.
SIX! What a lovely shot! A length ball, around off, Babar shimmies down the track and sends it over long off!
Short and outside off, cut through point where Reeza Hendricks dives to his right and makes a brilliant stop.
Full and around off, pushed towards point for a quick one.
Full and around middle, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
9TH T20I FIFTY FOR BABAR. This one comes off 34 balls. A length ball around off, worked wide of long on for a couple.
Andile Phehlukwayo into the attack.
Similar ball, worked wide of long on for just one.
Full and around off, spinning in, watchfully blocked out.
Short and outside off, punched through point for a run.
Full and around leg stump, Azam comes down the track and works it through square leg for a single.
Floated around off, watchfully defended.
Full and around middle, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
A short ball, outside off, pulled wide of long on for one. A quiet over.
Full and around middle, whipped through mid-wicket for a run. Talat moves to 10 from 5 balls.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Bowling. Lands it on a good length outside off, Azam looks to steer it to third man but almost nicks it behind. A different hat-trick for Babar this time - of dots.
Slower again, no pace on it, fuller in length, driven straight to cover.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Lutho Sipamla returns. 1-0-5-0 so far.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. One run added to the total. 70/1 IN THE POWERPLAY. This is some start. 119 more needed from 84 balls now.

Full and outside off, BA comes down the track and hammers it towards mid off. The batsmen think about the single and Junior Dala charges in. The batters change their mind and a worried Shamsi tells to Dala, 'EASY! EASY!'
Around middle and off, Babar looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a run.

EDGED, BUT NO SLIP! FOUR! Beautiful bowling from Shamsi. Flighted outside off, Talat looks to swing but the ball spins away and takes the outside edge. Straight to first slip. But there is no one there. Races to the third man fence.
Around middle, worked past short fine leg for a single.
Big gamble. Tabraiz Shamsi has been given the ball, with one over of the Powerplay left.
FOUR! That is through! Full on middle and leg, Talat flicks it through mid-wicket. Chris Morris jogs to his left, puts in a full-stretched dive but is nowhere near the ball! 18 from the over.
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
WIDE. Down the leg side, Talat fails to get it away.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.

FOUR! THIRD OCCASION OF BABAR HITTING A HAT-TRICK OF BOUNDARIES TODAY. First, of Beuran Hendricks. Then Chris Morris. Now, Junior Dala. A length ball, outside off, Azam punches this through the covers and gets his 9TH BOUNDARY!
FOUR! Bad line. It is fast and furious, at 140 kph, but the line is outside leg. Too full as well and Babar flicks it past short fine leg. 50 UP FOR PAKISTAN! 136 more needed from 94 balls.
FOUR! IMPERIOUS! Short and around off, Azam welcomes Dala nicely with a pull through mid-wicket!
Hussain Talat walks in at number 3, replacing Zaman. Junior Dala to bowl as well.

OUT! Caught at the boundary! Fakhar cannot believe it. He has literally thrown his wicket away. Not off a top edge, nor off an outside edge but holing out in the deep. A short ball and Zaman instinctively goes for the pull. Hits it well too. But to his dismay, he finds deep mid-wicket to perfection. Does not have to move an inch. FZ is disappointed but his team is off to a flier. 144 more needed from 96 balls. 10 from the over but a wicket for Hendricks. 2-0-24-1 so far.

FOUR! Bisection to perfection. A length ball outside off, Zaman cuts it nicely and so nicely that short third man gets across to his left, backward point to his right but yet, the ball goes right in between!
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side. One run added to the total.
On a length outside off, Azam chases after it and nearly edges it behind.
Outside off, cracked through the covers for a single.
FOUR! Change of ends but not change in intent from Pakistan! A length ball on middle, Zaman lofts it cleanly over mid on and gets a boundary!
Change of ends for Beuran Hendricks. 1-0-14-0 from the other end.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket. A very good start from the debutant. Just 5 from the opening over.
Full on middle and off, pushed down the ground for one more.
Down the leg side, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.

London bridge is falling down, falling down, falling down... South Africa rarely misfield and here we have seen two misfields on one ball. Zaman pushes it straight back to the bowler. Sipamla gets down to stop but misses. Chris Morris then gets across to his right and dives, but over the ball. David Miller mops it up from mid off, running backwards. Just a run but a comedy of errors.
Outside off, on a length, placed towards point for a run.
Full and around middle, worked towards Chris Morris at mid on for a quick single.
Big moment for the debutant. South Africa have got off to a poor start and Lutho Sipamla has been thrown from the frying pan into the fire.
Slower ball, fuller in length, worked wide of mid-wicket for a couple. 14 from the first, 16 from the second. Mount 189 looks scalable now...
FOUR! Babar gets a hat-trick again! This time against Morris. Overpitched, around off, Azam drives this straight back to where it came from. Mid on dives to his left but in vain.
FOUR! Now to the other side! A short ball, around middle, Azam pulls it fine of short fine leg! Moves to 21 from 8 balls with 5 fours!

FOUR! That was nicely bowled. Full and outside off, moving away, Babar hangs his bat out to dry and is squared up slightly. The ball goes off the outside edge past slip and with third man, the ball goes down fine.
Fuller and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Outside off, Fakhar punches this wide of mid off and without any hesitation, calls for a quick single. Makes it easily.
WIDE. Full and down the leg side, Zaman misses his flick. Good diving take by Heinrich Klaasen to his right.
Chris Morris to bowl from the other end.
Around middle and leg, worked wide of mid on to get off the mark with a run. 14 from the opening over is not a bad way to begin you mount of 189.
Full and around off, pushed down the ground. Mid on and mid off get across and one of them stops the ball. A single taken.
Outside off, lesser width this time, Azam looks to punch again but gets a thick inside edge, which just misses the stumps towards fine leg.
FOUR! A hat-trick! Beuran goes fuller outside off and Babar drives this wide of mid off, through the covers! Pakistan are up and running. 177 more needed from 117 balls.
FOUR! HAMMERED! Short and outside off, Azam punches it through the covers and gets boundaries in succession!
FOUR! An edge to start the run chase! A length ball outside off, Babar slashes hard and gets a thick outside edge which flies over a leaping first slip to the third man fence!

Oh my. The coffee that I started to brew is not even ready. Was that even a break? The Saffas are in a huddle. Out come the Pakistan openers. Babar Azam and Fakhar Zaman. Beuran Hendricks will start off proceedings to Babar. Here we go!
